Find the stationary point $B$ of the curve $y = x^2 - 4x + 7$ by setting the derivative to zero:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x - 4 = 0 \implies x = 2$$
$$y = 2^2 - 4(2) + 7 = 3 \implies B = (2, 3)$$

Substitute $(3, 5)$ into the line equation $y = mx - 2$ to find $m$:
$$5 = m(3) - 2 \implies 3m = 7 \implies m = \frac{7}{3}$$

Equate the curve and straight line equations to find points of intersection:
$$x^2 - 4x + 7 = mx - 2 \implies x^2 - (m + 4)x + 9 = 0$$

For the line not to meet the curve, the quadratic equation must have no real roots, requiring a strictly negative discriminant ($\Delta < 0$):
$$\Delta = [-(m + 4)]^2 - 4(1)(9) < 0$$
$$(m + 4)^2 - 36 < 0 \implies (m + 4)^2 < 36$$
$$-6 < m + 4 < 6$$
$$-10 < m < 2 \quad (\text{or } (-10, 2))$$
